name: Mieders
kurzbeschreibung: Welcome to the Stubaital gateway, featuring a summer sledding run, climbing park, and natural lake swimming area – perfect for family outings.
text:
Overview

Mieders lies at the entrance to the Stubaital on a sunny terraced slope at an altitude of 952 meters, approximately 15 kilometers south of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck. The village is home to around 1,950 residents and has preserved its authentic, rural charm despite its proximity to the Innsbruck urban area. Mieders is dominated by the striking limestone pyramid of the Serles (2,717 m), famously praised by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe during his Italian journey as the 'High Altar of Tyrol'. The municipal territory extends from the Ruetz river valley up to the craggy peaks of the Serles range. Mieders blends traditional Alpine farming with gentle, family-oriented year-round tourism, serving as an ideal gateway for nature lovers seeking mountain tranquility without overwhelming crowds.

History

Settlement around Mieders predates written history, evidenced by pre-Roman toponyms and archaeological traces. The first definitive written mention dates back to 1212 as 'Miders', deriving from ancient pre-Roman linguistic roots that indicate unbroken settlement continuity. For centuries, agriculture, cattle farming, and forestry formed the economic foundation of the local population. At the same time, Mieders benefited from its convenient location close to the vital Brenner pass transit route. The architectural centerpiece of the village center is the late Gothic parish church of the Nativity of Mary (Mariä Geburt), originating in the 14th century. In the 18th century, it was lavishly remodeled in Rococo style under the guidance of renowned Tyrolean builder-priest Franz de Paula Penz. With its slender, prominent spire and beautiful interior frescoes, the church ranks among the finest sacred monuments in the Wipptal and Stubaital regions.

Getting There

Reaching Mieders is quick and straightforward thanks to its location right at the gateway to the Stubaital. By car from Innsbruck, drivers take the A13 Brenner Autobahn to exit Schönberg/Stubaital, continuing onto the B183 Stubaitalstraße for just a few minutes until reaching the signposted turnoff for Mieders. A toll-free alternative runs along the B182 Brenner federal road. Rail passengers arrive at Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, where regular direct buses (Stubaitalbus route 590) operate frequently to Mieders village center and the Serlesbahnen valley terminal. The public transit ride takes merely 25 to 30 minutes, making Mieders particularly appealing for sustainable, car-free mountain excursions.

Tips

An absolute highlight for thrill-seekers and families is the Mieders Alpine Coaster at the Serlesbahnen. With a run of 2.8 kilometers, a vertical drop of 640 meters, and speeds reaching up to 42 km/h through 40 steep turns, it is celebrated as one of the steepest summer toboggan runs in the entire Alpine arc. At the Koppeneck mountain terminal (1,600 m), the Serleswasser recreation world beckons with refreshing shallow alpine ponds, play streams, and sun terraces. From Koppeneck, scenic hiking trails lead directly to the historic pilgrimage sanctuary of Maria Waldrast, the highest monastery pilgrimage site in Austria. In winter, the Serles slopes become a cozy family ski area featuring groomed pistes, panoramic winter walking trails, and exciting natural toboggan runs away from noisy resort crowds.
